typescript-engineer: A TypeScript engineer with expertise in Node.js development, TypeScript strict mode, and modern JavaScript/TypeScript features. Must be familiar with ES modules, type annotations, and build configurations. Should understand how to work with package.json, tsconfig.json, and vitest for testing. Must ensure all dependencies in package.json use exact versions (no version ranges) and strictly enforce TypeScript compiler options including 'strict' and 'strictNullChecks' set to true. Must properly configure vitest.config.ts with test.globals set to true. Must validate file paths and directory structures according to project requirements. When creating vitest.config.ts with test.globals: true, must ensure proper configuration to avoid test scope pollution or missing global variables. With strict mode enabled, must handle all strict mode implications including strictNullChecks, strictFunctionTypes, and others to prevent compilation errors. With module='CommonJS' in tsconfig.json, should ensure all imports/exports follow CommonJS patterns and avoid mixing with ES modules to prevent runtime issues. When creating package.json, must not create any references to 'index.ts' or 'index.js' as the real entry point is src/server.ts. Must use exact versions for all dependencies in package.json without version ranges or aliases. When writing vitest.config.ts, use ESM import/export syntax (import defineConfig from 'vitest/config'; export default defineConfig(...)) even though tsconfig.json specifies module='CommonJS' — Vitest processes vitest.config.ts with its own esbuild bundler, not tsc, so ESM syntax is required. Never use require() or module.exports in vitest.config.ts. In vitest.config.ts, must set test.passWithNoTests: true to ensure 'vitest run' exits 0 even when no test files exist — this is required for the scaffold phase where no tests have been written yet. In package.json, the 'main' field MUST be exactly 'dist/server.js' — never 'dist/index.js' or 'index.js'. The real entry point is src/server.ts which will be built by a later story. Do NOT create src/index.ts or any file named index.ts/index.js anywhere in the project. In package.json, 'express' MUST be listed under 'dependencies' (not 'devDependencies') because it is a runtime dependency. All dev-only packages (typescript, tsx, vitest, @types/express, @types/node) go under 'devDependencies'. Do NOT install any package whose name contains 'skyscanner', 'rapidapi', or any Skyscanner SDK — the project calls RapidAPI directly via Node.js global fetch (no third-party HTTP library). The only HTTP mechanism is the built-in global fetch available in Node 18+. Must create .gitignore at the project root with at minimum entries for 'node_modules' and 'dist'. The .gitignore file is required by acceptance criteria even though it is not listed in the technicalNotes.files array. Must create the src/ directory even if it contains no files initially — the acceptance criteria require it to exist. Use mkdir -p or equivalent. When running npm install, use --save-exact flag (or npm config set save-exact true) to ensure all dependency versions in package.json are pinned without ^ or ~ prefixes. For example, 'express' should appear as '"express": "4.18.2"' not '"express": "^4.18.2"'. The project runs on Node.js v20.20.0 (path: ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/node). When running tsc or vitest commands for verification, use the full path or ensure nvm has loaded the correct version. The acceptance criteria specify running '~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/node ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit' and '~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/node ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run'. package.json 'scripts' must contain EXACTLY: build='tsc', test='vitest run', start='node dist/server.js', dev='tsx src/server.ts'. Do not add extra scripts or modify these values. The 'start' script is 'node dist/server.js' because src/server.ts will be created by a later story (SKY-004). When using the Node.js global fetch (available in Node 18+), do NOT import from 'node-fetch' for type definitions — this conflicts with the global fetch types and causes TS7022 cascading errors. Use the built-in global fetch type declarations from @types/node (which is already a devDependency). If you need to type the Response object, use the global 'Response' type directly. When mocking global fetch with vi.stubGlobal('fetch', mockFn), the mock function must be explicitly typed to avoid noImplicitAny errors. Use: vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn() as unknown as typeof fetch) or provide an explicit return type on the mock function matching the Response type. When checking MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API environment variable for mock mode, use strict equality: process.env.MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API === 'true'. Do NOT use truthy checks like if (process.env.MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API) — values like 'false', '1', 'TRUE' must NOT activate mock mode. Only the exact string 'true' activates it. When throwing errors from searchFlights on HTTP 4xx/5xx, the error message must NOT include the apiKey value anywhere — this is a security requirement. Include the HTTP status code but never the API key. The SkyscannerClient constructor accepts { apiKey?: string }. An empty string ('') must be treated the same as undefined — throw the missing-key Error. The check must be: if (!apiKey) (covers undefined, empty string, and falsy values). The constructor-provided apiKey takes precedence over RAPIDAPI_KEY env var when both are present. In CLI code (src/cli.ts), write error messages to process.stderr using process.stderr.write() — not console.error(). This ensures test spies on process.stderr can capture output reliably. Use process.exit(1) or process.exit(2) for error exits as specified in acceptance criteria. The CLI (src/cli.ts) must parse arguments manually from process.argv — do NOT install commander, yargs, or any other argument-parsing library. Zero new runtime dependencies are allowed beyond what package.json already contains. When handling optional numeric query parameters in Express routes (e.g., 'adults'), you must explicitly narrow the type: check if the value is undefined before parsing, and validate that parseInt/Number produces a valid integer > 0. Do not pass number|undefined where number is required without explicit type narrowing — TypeScript strict mode will flag this. In src/server.ts, the listen() call must be guarded so importing 'app' in tests does not bind a port. Since the project uses CommonJS module output (module='CommonJS' in tsconfig.json), use: if (require.main === module) { app.listen(...) }. Do NOT use import.meta.url guard — that is ESM-only and will cause a runtime error in CommonJS output. In src/server.ts, the FlightResult type MUST be imported from src/skyscanner/client.ts (the SKY-002 export) — never redeclared inline. Type definitions must not diverge between the client and server layers. The build script must copy src/public/ into dist/public/ because tsc alone does not copy non-.ts files. The GET / route handler reads index.html at runtime via fs.readFileSync, so the file must exist at the correct path both under tsx src/server.ts (dev) and node dist/server.js (built). Consider adding a copy step to the build script (e.g., 'tsc && cp -r src/public dist/public' or using a package like shx). The RAPIDAPI_KEY check middleware must only gate /search and /cheapest routes — GET /health and GET / must always return 200 regardless of whether RAPIDAPI_KEY is set. Place the middleware after the /health and / route handlers, or use route-specific middleware. Do NOT use 'npm init -y' to create package.json — it defaults 'main' to 'index.js' which violates acceptance criteria. Write package.json manually or if using npm init -y, immediately change 'main' to 'dist/server.js' and remove any 'index.js' reference. tsconfig.json must include 'moduleResolution: node10' (or 'node') in compilerOptions. Without it, TypeScript cannot resolve node_modules correctly under CommonJS, causing tsc --noEmit to fail. tsconfig.json must set 'rootDir: src' in compilerOptions. This prevents tsc from trying to compile vitest.config.ts (which uses ESM syntax and is processed by Vitest's esbuild, not tsc). Without rootDir, tsc --noEmit will fail on vitest.config.ts's ESM import/export. tsconfig.json must include 'include: ["src"]' to scope compilation to the src/ directory only. This ensures tsc does not attempt to compile files outside src/. Before running npm install, run 'npm config set save-exact true' to ensure all dependency versions are pinned without ^ or ~ prefixes. After install, verify package.json contains no ^ or ~ version prefixes. When verifying the build, use the EXACT commands from acceptance criteria: ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/node ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit and ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/node ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run. Do NOT use npx tsc or npx vitest — these may resolve to a different Node version. Do NOT add 'type: module' to package.json. The project uses CommonJS module system (module='CommonJS' in tsconfig.json). Adding 'type: module' would cause runtime errors with the CommonJS output. In vitest.config.ts, set test.include to ['src/**/*.test.ts'] to ensure vitest only discovers test files in the src/ directory. This prevents vitest from finding stray .test.ts files elsewhere. tsconfig.json must include 'esModuleInterop: true' and 'allowSyntheticDefaultImports: true' in compilerOptions. Without these, importing CommonJS packages like express with 'import express from express' syntax will fail under strict mode. tsconfig.json must include 'skipLibCheck: true' in compilerOptions to avoid spurious type errors from third-party declaration files in node_modules. During the scaffold phase (SKY-001), do NOT create src/server.ts or any other .ts source file in src/. The src/ directory must exist but be empty — source files are created by subsequent stories. Creating a placeholder server.ts would conflict with SKY-004 which owns that file. The only files to create are: package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, .gitignore, and the empty src/ directory. Do NOT add a 'types' field to tsconfig.json compilerOptions. Setting types: ['node'] would prevent TypeScript from auto-discovering @types/express and other @types packages in node_modules. Omit the 'types' field entirely — TypeScript will automatically discover all packages under node_modules/@types/. Do NOT add a 'lib' field to tsconfig.json compilerOptions. Let TypeScript infer the default lib from the 'target' setting (ES2022 defaults to ['ES2022']). Explicitly setting lib could exclude type definitions needed by later stories (e.g., DOM types for the HTML dashboard). Do NOT add 'sourceMap: true', 'declaration: true', 'declarationMap: true', or 'composite: true' to tsconfig.json compilerOptions. These are not required for this project and would add unnecessary output files to the dist/ directory or impose additional compilation constraints. Execution order is critical: (1) Create package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, .gitignore, and src/ directory. (2) Run 'npm config set save-exact true'. (3) Run 'npm install'. (4) Verify package.json has no ^ or ~ prefixes. (5) Run tsc --noEmit verification. (6) Run vitest run verification. Do NOT attempt to run tsc --noEmit before npm install — it will fail because node_modules does not exist yet and TypeScript cannot resolve type packages. The .gitignore file must include at minimum 'node_modules' and 'dist' per acceptance criteria. Additionally, include '.env' and '.env.*' entries to prevent accidental commit of API keys and secrets. This is a security best practice even though not explicitly required by acceptance criteria. When loading the correct Node.js version for verification commands, use: 'source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use v20.20.0' or use the full path '~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/node' directly. Do NOT assume 'node' in PATH points to v20.20.0 — it may point to a system Node version. Do NOT add 'type: module', 'exports', 'module', or 'typings' fields to package.json. The project uses CommonJS module system (module='CommonJS' in tsconfig.json). Adding 'type: module' would cause runtime errors. The 'exports' and 'module' fields are not needed for this project structure. After completing all file creation and npm install, systematically verify EACH acceptance criterion: (1) package.json exists with name='skyscanner-app', (2) scripts match exactly, (3) main='dist/server.js', (4) express in dependencies, (5) all devDependencies present, (6) no skyscanner/rapidapi SDK, (7) tsconfig.json with all required compilerOptions, (8) vitest.config.ts with defineConfig and test.globals=true, (9) .gitignore with node_modules and dist, (10) src/ directory exists, (11) node_modules exists, (12) tsc --noEmit exits 0, (13) vitest run exits 0, (14) no reference to index.ts/index.js in package.json. tsconfig.json target MUST be exactly 'ES2022' — not 'ES2020', 'ES2021', 'ESNext', or any other value. ES2022 is required because the project uses Node.js 20 which fully supports ES2022 features including top-level await (in ESM) and the global fetch API. Using a lower target would cause TypeScript to downcompile features that Node 20 natively supports. CRITICAL: When running npm commands (npm install, npm config), use the full path ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/npm — NOT bare "npm". The system PATH resolves to a different Node version (v24.14.1 via fnm), and running bare "npm install" would install packages against the wrong Node ABI, causing binary compatibility failures. All npm commands must be: ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/npm install, ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/npm config set save-exact true, etc. CRITICAL: The target directory /home/bradleyjerome/projects/skyscanner-app ALREADY EXISTS with a .git repository and orchestration files (agent-activity.jsonl, step-status.json, spec-baseline.json, etc.). test-engineer: A test engineer specializing in unit testing with Vitest. Must be proficient in writing comprehensive test suites, mocking dependencies, and understanding test coverage. Should understand how to properly structure test files and use Vitest's features like vi.spyOn, vi.stubGlobal, and mock implementations. This agent ONLY writes test files - never implementation files. When writing test files, must follow the *.test.ts naming convention and place them in the src/ directory. When using vi.stubGlobal for fetch or other globals, must provide typed parameters to avoid noImplicitAny errors. Project: skyscanner-app. Test framework: vitest (configured in vitest.config.ts with test.globals: true, so describe/it/expect/vi/beforeEach/afterEach are available as globals without importing). Module system: CommonJS (tsconfig module='CommonJS'). Test files follow *.test.ts naming convention and are placed in src/ directory alongside implementation files. When mocking modules, use vi.mock('path/to/module') with the import path matching the module's location relative to the test file. When mocking global fetch, use vi.stubGlobal('fetch', mockFn) with explicitly typed mock parameters to avoid noImplicitAny errors. When testing environment variable behavior, use vi.stubEnv('VAR_NAME', value) and restore with vi.restoreAllMocks() in afterEach. This agent ONLY writes test files — never implementation files. Never modify package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, or any scaffold-phase infrastructure file. When testing MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API behavior, verify that only the exact string 'true' activates mock mode — test with 'false', '1', 'TRUE', empty string, and undefined to confirm they all result in real fetch calls. When testing CLI output, spy on process.stderr.write and process.stdout.write rather than console.error/console.log — the CLI implementation uses process.stderr.write for errors. Use vi.spyOn(process.stderr, 'write') and vi.spyOn(process.stdout, 'write'). When testing Express routes with supertest, import the named 'app' export from src/server.ts — do NOT start the server with listen(). Use vi.mock('../skyscanner/client') to mock SkyscannerClient so no real HTTP calls are made. Test both the happy path and error paths (client throws, empty results, missing RAPIDAPI_KEY).
